Good day. This is Sultana Al-Qahtani with the Sahel Desk.

Bottom line: the latest collection cycle retained 11 new relevant reports. The fusion layer recorded no newly created fused event IDs. The archive currently contains 10 candidate events in the last seven days and 35 in the last thirty days.

Country-by-country reporting:
Mali: 2 retained reports in the latest cycle; no current-cycle article rows were available to narrate.
Burkina Faso: 3 retained reports in the latest cycle.
Burkina Faso report 1: Burkina Faso's military leaders mark four years in power. Summary: People gathered in Ougadougou’s Place de la Révolution on Wednesday night to mark four years since Captain Ibrahim Traoré came to power in a coup. The culmination of anniversary celebrations, they paid tribute to the armed forces and the military government’s achievements in Burkina Faso. One resident, Abdoul Rasmané Sawadogo, said military leaders have created an “ultra-modern army that meets expectations”.
Burkina Faso report 2: Pix of the Day, 30 September, 2026 - Across the world. Summary: Burkina Faso has inaugurated its first gold refinery as its military-led government seeks to strengthen economic sovereignty after breaking ties with its traditional Western partners. “From now on, Burkina Faso’s gold must not only be mined in Burkina Faso; it must also be processed, controlled, valued and certified there,” President Ibrahim Traoré said on Monday at the inauguration of the refinery, named Raffinor-BF.
Burkina Faso report 3: Crash of the Ouagadougou-Alger flight: Swiftair condemned. Summary: The families of the victims had to wait twelve years. Gathered within the association "AH-5017 Ensemble", they led a "relentless fight for truth and justice" which is now experiencing its judicial outcome. The Spanish company Swiftair is found guilty of manslaughter this Monday morning by the Paris Criminal Court .
Niger: 6 retained reports in the latest cycle.
Niger report 1: Drug trafficking: two young people in their twenties arrested with 12,000 Tramadol tablets at the Tillabéri road barrier. Summary: Published on Tuesday, December 30, 2025 | actuniger.com The vigilance of the security forces has once again borne fruit . On December 22, 2025, officers of the Yantala Police Station seized 12,000 Tramadol tablets during a routine check at the Tillabéri road barrier, thwarting an attempt to transport drugs to a gold site in the region, with the arrest of two young Nigeriens in their twenties .
Niger report 2: Niger: what we know about the jihadist attack that targeted Niamey airport. Summary: Niger: what we know about the jihadist attack that targeted the Niamey airport Published on Saturday, January 31, 2026 | AFP In the night from Wednesday to Thursday, the Niamey airport in Niger suffered a brief attack claimed Friday by the Islamic State, in a country where jihadist violence usually occurs in the west and south-east The Nigerien military junta, helped by "Russian partners", accused the French, Beninese and Ivorian presidents of being the "sponsors" of the attackers, words condemned by Abidjan and Cotonou on Friday.
Niger report 3: Defence: General Tiani reshuffles the military command after the Niamey mutiny. Summary: Defense: General Tiani reshuffles the military command after the Niamey mutiny Published on Saturday, September 12, 2026 | actuniger.com Two weeks to the day after the Niamey mutiny, the President of the Republic and Supreme Chief of the Armed Forces, General Abdourahamane Tiani, Supreme Chief of the Armed Forces, reshuffled the head of the Niger army on Friday, September 11, 2026 According to a statement from the Ministry of National Defence read in the evening on public television, the post of Chief of the Armed Forces Staff (CEMA), Major General Moussa Salaou Barmou, a member of the CNSP and in office since…

articles.title: Niger: Islamic State claims responsibility for attack on Niamey airport
articles.summary: Published on Friday, January 30, 2026 | AFP The Islamic State claimed responsibility on Friday for the attack on Niamey airport in Niger, said the Site group, which specializes in counter-terrorism research . On the night of Wednesday to Thursday, Niamey airport, which is home to military sites and is about ten kilometers from the presidency, was the target of an attack leaving 20 dead on the attacking side, according to the Nigerien military junta .
